chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Jamīlah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no harm for the traveler to perform the prayer in full during travel of two days’ journey. This report also accords with the generality, and we do not act upon it, because that in which shortening is obligatory is the measure that we mentioned, whether it is a journey of two days or less or more. And it is possible that the report is to be understood as applying to one who travels in two days less than the amount in which shortening is obligatory; then, in that case, completing the prayer becomes obligatory upon him. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is:

key_terms.أَنْ يُتِمَّ: to complete; to perform the salat (prayer) in full rather than shortened form
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the salat (prayer) due to travel
key_terms.فِي السَّفَرِ: during travel; in the state of journeying
key_terms.لِلْمُسَافِرِ: for the traveler; the person subject to the rulings of travel
key_terms.مَحْمُولًا: interpreted as; understood in a particular legal sense
key_terms.مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمَيْنِ: a journey of two days; a measure mentioned in the report
key_terms.يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ التَّمَامُ: full prayer becomes obligatory upon him; he must not shorten

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler shorten the salat (prayer), and how is a two-day journey report understood in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the fiqh ruling of a traveler’s prayer and addresses a report ظاهرُه indicates permissibility of completing the prayer on a two-day journey. The text states that such a report is not acted upon in its apparent sense, since the criterion for taqsir is the legally defined distance, whether covered in two days, less, or more, and it may instead refer to a case where the traveled distance does not reach the amount requiring shortening.
